chapter.title: Introduction
chapter.para: RexxHTTP is a rexxlet processor for &Rexx; and Apache. It runs as a CGI program under the Apache HTTP server: Apache hands it an incomingRexxHTTPrexxlet processorrexxletCGIApache request, and RexxHTTP turns the raw CGI environment into a small set of objects, runs the rexxlet against them, and writes the result back as an HTTP response. A rexxlet is an ordinary &Rexx; program, so the whole of &Rexx; is available to it, with the HTTP request and the response it is about to build handed in as objects instead of being read out of environment variables by hand.

For each request RexxHTTP builds three objects. A request object exposes the request line,requestrequest objectresponseresponse objectoutput streambufferinglazy headersheaderscookiestatus linecommitbody.request.response the headers and the GET/POST arguments through named methods, decoding percent- and plus-escapes automatically. A response object collects the status line and the response headers, cookies among them, and allows them to be attached. And an output stream receives the body: it is a buffering subclass of the built-in Stream class, which allows the response headers to be written lazily: status, headers and cookies may still be changed after the body has been started, up to the point where the response is committed. The request and the response reach the rexxlet as the .request and .response objects, placed in the environment by RexxHTTP. The body is produced with the ordinary SAY instruction or the CHAROUT function. The response is committed on the first flush, which normally happens when the rexxlet ends. The chapter describes this model in detail.

chapter.para: RexxHTTP requires &Rexx; 5.3.0 r13572 or later and Apache 2.4 or later. It is released under the Apache License 2.0 and published at https://rexx.epbcn.com/rexxhttp/ and on GitHub at https://github.com/JosepMariaBlasco/RexxHTTP. The first is preferred, because it uses the Rexx Highlighter to colour its program listings.
